answer: Standing comes through a chain of 120 lantern rounds. Each round shows an ambiguous image — a shadow shared by two objects — asking which object cast it; the next image follows the answer just given and the applicant's own key, so no round opens early. Three graders score each answer; one miss breaks it. An umber stamp marks each passed round on the anchor card, bound to that applicant alone. One chain takes 6 hours of human looking, $48; 5,000 fakes need 30,000 hours and $240,000. Looking will not divide: one mind per round, rounds never run together, no bulk order shortens one.
